trajectory_summary: This is a short, purely administrative reschedule call following a no-show/miscommunication at the door. The rep never re-runs verify, interest, bill, or qualifier sections — the entire call is spent locating the account, explaining the missed appointment, and locking a new time. The call ends with a booked day and time, but with none of the standard setter script executed.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown, but observed outcome is booked (Monday at 5PM) — a clear day+time was captured with a mutual handshake, so if v1 called this anything other than booked/tentative it should be corrected.

observed_outcome.quote: I'll get that set for five, and we will shoot you a reminder text just to double check that time still works for you.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Monday) and time (5PM) were agreed and the rep confirmed he would set it up, meeting the bar for a booked outcome even though full button-up mechanics were skipped.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: This call is a pure reschedule of a previously missed appointment — no bill, usage, or utility information is discussed at any point in the transcript.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asks what interested the customer in solar; the call is treated entirely as a logistics/reschedule fix, presumably because this information was captured on a prior touch, but nothing on this call confirms or reuses it.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: I'll get that set for five, and we will shoot you a reminder text just to double check that time still works for you.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep locked a day and time but skipped the full confirmation protocol (hour block, no-driving/computer instruction, explicit fairness handshake) — on a call with a customer already juggling a tight personal schedule (track practice at 5:45), this is exactly the kind of appointment likely to soften or no-show without a firm procedural close.

key_moments.quote: Oh, and this is Pike with ION. Did you put in some information looking at solar for the home?
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep's intro is thin — no state mention, no clear framing of why he's calling beyond a vague reference to 'some information,' and it comes as an afterthought after the customer already had to explain themselves. This is a recontact call so some legitimacy work was already done at prior touch, but the rep still doesn't re-anchor identity/context cleanly.

key_moments.quote: It looks like, yeah, it looks like we we had time set up to share a solar design with you. It looks like a a, a week or so ago, that ended up falling through.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep surfaces that a rep (Jose) went to the door and the appointment fell through, but never asks the customer what actually happened or why no one answered — there's real information here (was it a bad time, disinterest, confusion) that goes uncollected.

key_moments.quote: But, yeah, we were just gonna one we were just wondering if there'd be a better time next week that would work for you.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep treats this purely as a logistics fix and never re-engages the customer's original interest in solar or their bill/usage situation — a full reschedule opportunity to re-anchor value is skipped.

key_moments.quote: the times we have available would be 09:30, 12PM, 02:30, 5PM, and 07:30PM.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer has a hard constraint (track practice at 5:45) right up against the 5PM slot chosen, and the rep only lightly acknowledges it ('That's fine... should be fine') without building in buffer or confirming with the closer team that this is a tight window.
